### Derivation Strategy

The total count $C$ is the sum of counts for red triples ($N_R$) and blue triples ($N_B$).
$$C = N_R + N_B$$

$N_R$ is the number of triples $(x, y, z) \in S \times S \times S$ such that $x, y, z$ are red and $x+y+z \equiv 0 \pmod n$.

We use the standard technique of counting solutions modulo $n$ using the $n$-th roots of unity. Let $\omega = e^{2\pi i / n}$. The number of solutions to $x+y+z \equiv 0 \pmod n$ where $x, y, z$ are restricted by properties related to residue classes $k$ is given by:
$$N_R = \sum_{k_x, k_y, k_z \in \{0, \ldots, n-1\}, k_x+k_y+k_z \equiv 0 \pmod n} r_{k_x} r_{k_y} r_{k_z}$$

Using the orthogonality property of roots of unity:
$$\frac{1}{n} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} \omega^{j(k_x+k_y+k_z)} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } k_x+k_y+k_z \equiv 0 \pmod n \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

We substitute this into the expression for $N_R$:
$$N_R = \sum_{k_x, k_y, k_z} r_{k_x} r_{k_y} r_{k_z} \cdot \frac{1}{n} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} \omega^{j(k_x+k_y+k_z)}$$
